text:
olivia: seeing a spike of TCP resets from model-cache svc in eu-south1. Pods reporting Readiness probe failures, p99 latency jumps, and lots of short-lived outbound connections. Noticed conntrack table ~95% full on NAT nodes.

ben_oncall: yikes. which NATs? metrics?

olivia: nat-gw-3 and nat-gw-4 in eu-south1. grafana: conntrack_count per node -> 388k / 400k. ephemeral-port-utilization also near 64k.

kevin: can you paste a conntrack dump snippet? also any recent rollout to model workers?

olivia: dump excerpt below:
```
# conntrack -L | tail -n 6
tcp      6 29 ESTABLISHED src=10.10.2.45 dst=10.11.3.12 sport=51632 dport=8080 src=10.11.3.12 dst=10.10.2.45 sport=8080 dport=51632 [ASSURED] mark=0
tcp      6 29 SYN_SENT src=10.10.2.47 dst=10.11.3.12 sport=51635 dport=8080 src=10.11.3.12 dst=10.10.2.47 sport=8080 dport=51635 [UNREPLIED]
```

maria: any change in client connection behavior? we had a recent change to scale-to-zero on some model proxies last week, could be chattier reconnections.

olivia: yes — we rolled a scale-to-zero optimization for the model-proxy pod on 1748495000. That increases short-lived TCP churn to model-cache. Might be related.

ben_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) bump nf_conntrack_max on affected NAT nodes, 2) enable raw table NOTRACK for intra-cluster model-cache traffic, 3) temporarily pin model-proxy replicas (disable scale-to-zero). Which do we want now?

kevin: do 3) and 1) now. 2) is invasive to track/metrics.

olivia: applying pin and conntrack bump on nat-gw-3 first. Running commands now:
```
echo 524288 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
kubectl patch hpa model-proxy -n ml --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":3}]'
```

deploy-bot: rolling update started for deployment/model-proxy in namespace ml (revision v2 -> v3) :rocket:

ben_oncall: keep an eye on conntrack_count and tcp_retransmits. If that doesn't relieve, we'll add a NOTRACK rule for traffic to 10.11.3.0/24 (model-cache cluster ip range) on the NAT nodes.

maria: also recommend adding tcp_keepalive tweaks in model-proxy so connections last longer instead of reconnect bursts. I'll open a follow-up PR.

olivia: after bump + pin: conntrack on nat-gw-3 dropped to 42% used within 90s. readiness failures decreased. rollout seemed to help, p95 latency back to baseline.

kevin: great. still want a long-term fix: options = a) move model-cache to headless + keep-alive + connection pooling, b) mark model-cache traffic NOTRACK and use in-cluster iptables for visibility, c) implement eBPF SNAT pooling (like smaller ephemeral ranges per node), d) improve CNI SNAT behavior. Which path aligns with infra roadmap?

maria: infra roadmap includes eBPF SNAT experiments this quarter. but headless/connection-pool at app layer is fastest. we should do both: app change short term, eBPF pilot medium term.

ben_oncall: agree. create follow-up tickets: 1) APP-1872 - connection pooling + keepalive for model-proxy (owned by ML infra), 2) INFRA-3210 - eBPF SNAT pilot in eu-south1 (owned by networking), 3) RUN-4021 - add conntrack alarm + automated bump for burst windows.

olivia: making tickets now. also updating runbook to include pin + bump procedure and the threshold (conntrack > 85%).

deploy-bot: canary finished: 2/2 pods healthy.

kevin: leaving note: check RDMA-enabled instances — we saw similar port churn when RDMA fallback raced with TCP. If any models use RDMA fallback, add to risk note.

maria: noted. I'll add RDMA check to INFRA-3210 scope.

olivia: tl;dr: root cause = scale-to-zero change + high churn to model-cache causing SNAT/conntrack exhaustion on NAT nodes. Short-term: pinned replicas + nf_conntrack bump cleared incident. Medium-term: app pooling + eBPF SNAT pilot + runbook + alarms.

ben_oncall: closing for now — reopen if counts rise. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks all. great quick ops.

olivia: thanks — filing postmortem stub in incidents/ after I finish timeline.
